routes.description: The lifeline: the only 24h mainland–island link, ~12,584 users/day, 4–6h vehicle queues in season. Foiling shuttle flies it in ~3 minutes.
Mainland ferry head direct to Ilhabela's historic centre — today requires the balsa plus a bus/taxi along the island shore road.
Cross-channel diagonal to the Perequê Aquabus pier, the island stop closest to the crossing corridor.
Ferry head to the island's full-service marina — charter pickup and charging base on the channel.
Mainland to the Saco da Capela yacht cluster (YCI anchorage) — regatta crew and owner transfers in the sailing capital.
Northern channel diagonal: São Francisco marina shore straight to the historic centre — no service exists today.
Mainland coastal spur linking the north-shore marinas to the ferry head and town centre.
Marina-to-marina channel hop: São Francisco to Saco da Capela across the narrowest reach.
Aquabus segment: south-island terminus to the ferry pier at Barra Velha.
Aquabus segment: ferry pier to Perequê along the west shore.
Ferry arrivals straight to the historic centre by water — skipping the shore-road traffic that chokes summer weekends.
Aquabus segment: Perequê to Vila past Engenho D'Água.
Marina guests to the restaurants and nightlife of the historic village — short, silent, zero-wake.
The full Aquabus line modernised: Praia Grande–Perequê–Engenho D'Água–Vila along the sheltered west coast. 5.7 nm direct; ~6.3 nm with coastal hug between stops.
Mainland direct to south Ilhabela, bypassing the ferry and the island shore road entirely. 3.1 nm direct; ~3.4 nm keeping sea room off Ponta das Baleias.

The Castelhanos run: around Ponta das Canas to the boat-only Atlantic flagship beach. Legs 3.2 + 8.2 nm via the northern point plus ~15% coastal-wrap margin ⇒ ~13 nm. Served today by R$290–310/pax speedboat tours; weather-window operations on the exposed east side.

South-coast wilds spur to the caiçara village of Bonete. Legs 3.2 + 5.4 nm via Praia Grande plus ~20% wrap margin around Ponta da Sela ⇒ ~10.5 nm. Operator flex-boat tours run today; exposed to southerly swell — weather-window only.

Costa Verde link: Ilhabela's historic village to Paraty's UNESCO colonial harbour. 48.8 nm direct; routed around Ponta das Canas with sea-room margin ⇒ ~52 nm — inside the 70 nm electric envelope with reserve; shore charging needed at the Paraty end. Cross-market corridor to the Angra dos Reis–Paraty network.
